good heavens! interjection

also good grief, my goodness, goodness me, good Lord, heavens above, for heaven’s sake, good Lord!, in heaven’s name!

Cic. Att. 1.18.5: ō dī immortālēs! quam ignāvus ac sine animō mīles!

Dī immortālēs!

good heavens! (lit. immortal gods!)

(Cic. in epistulīs et ōrātiōnibus; Plaut.)

Also with ō or prō before it. Cicero’s commonest exclamation.

Other words

  • Prō dī immortālēs! — good heavens!

    also used · classical · Plaut. Curc. 274: Prō dī immortālēs, quem cōnspiciō? quis illic est?

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; also Cic. (Imp. Pomp. 33, Lewis & Short))

    Lewis & Short (s.v. prō interj.): “wonder or lamentation”.

  • Dī bonī! — good gods! my goodness!

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 14.9.2: ō dī bonī! vīvit tyrannis, tyrannus occidit!; Cic. Att. 1.14.4; Traupman 322

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Cic. in epistulīs)

  • Prō Juppiter! — good Lord! (by Jupiter)

    also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 1074: crēdō edepol, nam, prō Juppiter, sepultust quasi sit mortuos.

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

  • Prō deum atque hominum fidem! — for heaven’s sake! (indignation)

    also used · classical · Ter. And. 246: Prō deum atque hominum fidem!; Traupman 329

    (vōx cōmica: Ter.; also Cic. (Tusc. 5.48, Lewis & Short))

    An appeal to the protection of gods and men, said in outrage; for a real cry for help see help!.

  • Obsecrō! — for heaven’s sake! (literally, I beg you)

    first person of obsecrāre, used as an interjection · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 803: Au, obsecrō; Traupman 107: for heaven’s sake, obsecrō (lit. I pray); Traupman 327

    An appeal or an exclamation of dismay; see also please.

  • Per fortūnās! — for heaven’s sake! in heaven’s name!

    also used · classical · Traupman 327

Examples

  • Aulī autem fīlius, ō dī immortālēs! quam ignāvus ac sine animō mīles!

    And Aulus’s son, good heavens! what a cowardly, spiritless soldier!Cic. Att. 1.18.5

  • Prō dī immortālēs, quem cōnspiciō? quis illic est?

    Good heavens, who is that I see? who’s there?Plaut. Curc. 274

  • ō dī bonī! vīvit tyrannis, tyrannus occidit!

    Good gods! the tyranny lives, the tyrant is dead!Cic. Att. 14.9.2

  • crēdō edepol, nam, prō Juppiter, sepultust quasi sit mortuos.

    I believe it, by Pollux; for, good Lord, he’s buried as if he were dead.Plaut. Amph. 1074

  • Prō deum atque hominum fidem!

    For heaven’s sake!Ter. And. 246

See also well, well!, wow!, by Hercules!.
